name: realworld
description: Extended real-world dataset profile (SNAP edge lists from ../datasets): web-Google, wiki-Talk, soc-LiveJournal1, cit-Patents, cit-HepPh. Each traversal algorithm additionally runs on a DFS-preorder reordered copy (graphity-reordered pseudo-lib -> 'Graphity (reordered)' column), and the one-time reorder cost is captured by the graphity-only 'reorder' algorithm. Weakly connected components run on all five datasets; topological levelling only on cit-Patents, the only acyclic one, and there also on a bi-adjacent graph (graphity-biadjacent pseudo-lib -> 'Graphity (bi-adjacent)' column). The two structures behind those columns are priced separately: 'biadjacency' for Graphity's in-adjacency, 'symmetrize' for the symmetric BVGraph that WebGraph's ConnectedComponents requires. Perf-only: real-world allocation/memory footprint is out of scope here (footprint is topology-independent and already covered by the synthetic profiles). NOTE on jvm_stack/jvm_heap: the peer libraries use recursive DFS (JGraphT's Kosaraju, Guava port, and WebGraph's own StronglyConnectedComponents, whose Javadoc literally advises a large stack). On soc-LiveJournal1 (4.8M nodes, the largest of the five) they overflow the default stack; measured minimum -Xss to complete SCC is 256m (WebGraph) / 512m (Guava), while Graphity's iterative cores need none of this. -Xss512m + -Xmx64g clear all four libraries on all five datasets (combined cross-validation peaks at ~38 GB RSS on soc-LiveJournal1; the other four are all smaller and need less). Graphity alone would run at the default -Xss16m.
